papers.title: Paper-Based Biosensors for Monitoring Binding, Blocking, and Surrogate Neutralizing Antibody Responses Against Viral Infections
papers.abstract: Virus-specific antibody responses, including binding antibodies and neutralizing antibodies (nAbs), are important indicators of antiviral immune status after infection or immunization. They provide complementary information on antiviral humoral immunity after infection or vaccination. Antigen-binding antibodies indicate previous exposure and the magnitude of the immune response, whereas receptor-blocking and functional neutralization assays assess whether antibodies interfere with viral entry or infection. Conventional neutralization assays, such as plaque reduction neutralization tests and pseudovirus neutralization tests, provide functional information but are labor-intensive, time-consuming, biosafety-restricted, and difficult to deploy for large-scale or decentralized monitoring. Paper-based biosensors, including lateral flow assays (LFAs), microfluidic paper-based analytical devices (μPADs), and paper-based ELISA, have emerged as promising point-of-care tools owing to their low cost, portability, simple operation, and compatibility with visual or digital readouts. This review critically evaluates these platforms according to whether they measure antigen-binding antibodies, receptor-blocking activity, surrogate neutralization, or functional neutralization and summarizes the applications of these three platforms for monitoring antibody responses against SARS-CoV-2, influenza, dengue, Zika, and monkeypox viruses. Unlike previous reviews that mainly focus on general paper-based biosensor design or conventional nAb assays, this review emphasizes the distinction between antigen-binding, receptor-blocking, and surrogate neutralization readouts, and critically discusses how paper-based signals should be interpreted in relation to functional immunity. We further analyze key translational challenges, including quantitative accuracy, antigen cross-reactivity, standardization, clinical validation, regulatory positioning, and real-world implementation. Future development should combine multiplex detection, standardized calibration, digital and AI-assisted interpretation, and clinically validated assay formats. Paper-based biosensors have considerable potential for decentralized antibody monitoring and public health surveillance, but their clinical utility depends on clear assay positioning and validation against appropriate functional or reference methods.

papers.title_zh: 用于监测针对病毒感染的结合、阻断和替代中和抗体反应的纸基生物传感器
papers.source_body_en: Virus-specific antibody responses, including binding antibodies and neutralizing antibodies (nAbs), are important indicators of antiviral immune status after infection or immunization. They provide complementary information on antiviral humoral immunity after infection or vaccination. Antigen-binding antibodies indicate previous exposure and the magnitude of the immune response, whereas receptor-blocking and functional neutralization assays assess whether antibodies interfere with viral entry or infection. Conventional neutralization assays, such as plaque reduction neutralization tests and pseudovirus neutralization tests, provide functional information but are labor-intensive, time-consuming, biosafety-restricted, and difficult to deploy for large-scale or decentralized monitoring. Paper-based biosensors, including lateral flow assays (LFAs), microfluidic paper-based analytical devices (μPADs), and paper-based ELISA, have emerged as promising point-of-care tools owing to their low cost, portability, simple operation, and compatibility with visual or digital readouts. This review critically evaluates these platforms according to whether they measure antigen-binding antibodies, receptor-blocking activity, surrogate neutralization, or functional neutralization and summarizes the applications of these three platforms for monitoring antibody responses against SARS-CoV-2, influenza, dengue, Zika, and monkeypox viruses. Unlike previous reviews that mainly focus on general paper-based biosensor design or conventional nAb assays, this review emphasizes the distinction between antigen-binding, receptor-blocking, and surrogate neutralization readouts, and critically discusses how paper-based signals should be interpreted in relation to functional immunity. We further analyze key translational challenges, including quantitative accuracy, antigen cross-reactivity, standardization, clinical validation, regulatory positioning, and real-world implementation. Future development should combine multiplex detection, standardized calibration, digital and AI-assisted interpretation, and clinically validated assay formats. Paper-based biosensors have considerable potential for decentralized antibody monitoring and public health surveillance, but their clinical utility depends on clear assay positioning and validation against appropriate functional or reference methods.
papers.abstract_zh: 病毒特异性抗体反应,包括结合抗体和中和抗体(nAb),是感染或免疫后 抗病毒药物 免疫状态的重要指标。它们提供了感染后 抗病毒药物 体液免疫或 疫苗接种 的补充信息。抗原结合抗体表明之前的暴露情况和 免疫应答 的大小,而受体阻断和功能中和测定则评估抗体是否干扰病毒进入或感染。传统的中和测定,例如噬菌斑减少中和试验和假病毒中和试验,可以提供功能信息,但劳动密集型、耗时、生物安全性受限,并且难以部署用于大规模或分散监测。纸基生物传感器,包括侧流测定 (LFA)、微流控纸基分析装置 (μPAD) 和纸基 ELISA,由于其成本低、便携、操作简单以及与视觉或数字读数的兼容性,已成为有前途的护理点工具。本综述根据这些平台是否测量抗原结合抗体、受体阻断活性、替代中和或功能中和对这些平台进行了批判性评估,并总结了这三个平台在监测针对 SARS-CoV-2、流感、登革热、寨卡和猴痘病毒的抗体反应方面的应用。与之前主要关注一般纸质生物传感器设计或传统 nAb 测定的综述不同,本综述强调抗原结合、受体阻断和替代中和读数之间的区别,并批判性地讨论了如何解释与功能免疫相关的纸质信号。我们进一步分析关键的转化挑战,包括定量准确性、抗原交叉反应性、标准化、临床验证、监管定位和实际实施。未来的发展应结合多重检测、标准化校准、数字和人工智能辅助解释以及临床验证的检测格式。纸基生物传感器在分散抗体监测和公共卫生 监测 方面具有相当大的潜力,但其临床效用取决于明确的测定定位和针对适当功能或参考方法的验证。

papers.title: Operationalizing One Digital Health and FAIR Data Principles for Disease Surveillance in a Low-Medium Income Country in Africa: Qualitative Study in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Recent crises involving zoonotic diseases (Ebola, COVID-19, and Mpox) have highlighted the limitations of fragmented public health systems for the prevention and response to health emergencies at the international and continental level, and particularly in Africa, more specifically in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). In this context, the One Health (OH) approach and its extension, One Digital Health (ODH), articulated with the findable, accessible, interoperable, reusable (FAIR) principles, offer a framework for rethinking the digital transition in health in the DRC. This study analyzes the reality of this transition in Kinshasa, DRC, and questions the feasibility of ODH in this context. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to (1) explore how stakeholders across human, animal, and environmental health sectors perceive and experience digital tool integration and data interoperability in Kinshasa; (2) identify structural, institutional, and technical constraints affecting cross-sectoral data sharing; and (3) analyze the sociotechnical conditions required for the operationalization of ODH in a fragmented digital health (DH) context. METHODS: A qualitative study was conducted in Kinshasa, DRC, between November 10, 2025, and November 25, 2025, combining semistructured interviews with key actors (health professionals, administrative officials, digital experts, and engaged citizens) and a document review of strategic and regulatory texts related to DH in the DRC. The data were analyzed using a thematic approach to identify the representations, uses, and constraints related to DH and the operationalization of ODH. RESULTS: Overall, 22 stakeholders participated (n=9, 40.9% human health; n=8, 36.4% animal health; n=4, 18.2% environmental health; n=1, 4.50% digital sector), predominantly male (n=15, 68.2%) and mainly in operational roles (n=12, 54.5%). Three interrelated topics emerged. First, a dual-track digital ecosystem characterized by the coexistence of formal platforms (eg, District Health Information Software 2 and electronic records) and informal tools (eg, WhatsApp [Meta]), with persistent paper-digital double-entry generating inefficiencies. Second, structural and governance bottlenecks, including electricity instability, limited connectivity, software incompatibility, external data-hosting concerns that affect sovereignty, and institutional silos that privilege human health over animal and environmental sectors. Third, prerequisites for operationalizing ODH emphasize foundational infrastructure (energy and internet), sustainable capacity building beyond one-off training, interoperable "bridges" between fragmented systems, and high-level political leadership. These elements were synthesized into an ODH-FAIR DRC conceptual model structured around three enabling pillars linking sectors for integrated zoonotic surveillance. CONCLUSIONS: Operationalizing ODH in DRC requires addressing foundational enablers beyond tools: synchronized energy-digital policies, decompartmentalized governance, and context-adapted capacity building. These insights inform low- and middle-income countries' DH strategies, urging donors and ministries to prioritize interoperability over isolated pilots to achieve sustainable zoonotic surveillance.

papers.title_zh: 在非洲中低收入国家实施一种数字健康和公平疾病数据原则 监测:刚果民主共和国的定性研究。
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Recent crises involving zoonotic diseases (Ebola, COVID-19, and Mpox) have highlighted the limitations of fragmented public health systems for the prevention and response to health emergencies at the international and continental level, and particularly in Africa, more specifically in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). In this context, the One Health (OH) approach and its extension, One Digital Health (ODH), articulated with the findable, accessible, interoperable, reusable (FAIR) principles, offer a framework for rethinking the digital transition in health in the DRC. This study analyzes the reality of this transition in Kinshasa, DRC, and questions the feasibility of ODH in this context. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to (1) explore how stakeholders across human, animal, and environmental health sectors perceive and experience digital tool integration and data interoperability in Kinshasa; (2) identify structural, institutional, and technical constraints affecting cross-sectoral data sharing; and (3) analyze the sociotechnical conditions required for the operationalization of ODH in a fragmented digital health (DH) context. METHODS: A qualitative study was conducted in Kinshasa, DRC, between November 10, 2025, and November 25, 2025, combining semistructured interviews with key actors (health professionals, administrative officials, digital experts, and engaged citizens) and a document review of strategic and regulatory texts related to DH in the DRC. The data were analyzed using a thematic approach to identify the representations, uses, and constraints related to DH and the operationalization of ODH. RESULTS: Overall, 22 stakeholders participated (n=9, 40.9% human health; n=8, 36.4% animal health; n=4, 18.2% environmental health; n=1, 4.50% digital sector), predominantly male (n=15, 68.2%) and mainly in operational roles (n=12, 54.5%). Three interrelated topics emerged. First, a dual-track digital ecosystem characterized by the coexistence of formal platforms (eg, District Health Information Software 2 and electronic records) and informal tools (eg, WhatsApp [Meta]), with persistent paper-digital double-entry generating inefficiencies. Second, structural and governance bottlenecks, including electricity instability, limited connectivity, software incompatibility, external data-hosting concerns that affect sovereignty, and institutional silos that privilege human health over animal and environmental sectors. Third, prerequisites for operationalizing ODH emphasize foundational infrastructure (energy and internet), sustainable capacity building beyond one-off training, interoperable "bridges" between fragmented systems, and high-level political leadership. These elements were synthesized into an ODH-FAIR DRC conceptual model structured around three enabling pillars linking sectors for integrated zoonotic surveillance. CONCLUSIONS: Operationalizing ODH in DRC requires addressing foundational enablers beyond tools: synchronized energy-digital policies, decompartmentalized governance, and context-adapted capacity building. These insights inform low- and middle-income countries' DH strategies, urging donors and ministries to prioritize interoperability over isolated pilots to achieve sustainable zoonotic surveillance.

papers.title: Current Strategies for Selecting Recombinant Orthopoxvirus Proteins for Immunobiological and Diagnostic Applications
papers.abstract: Orthopoxviruses are zoonotic DNA viruses of continuing public health importance, as highlighted by recent global mpox outbreaks. The high antigenic similarity among orthopoxviruses enables cross-reactive immune responses but complicates the development of serological diagnostic systems for serosurveillance, assessment of previous exposure, evaluation of vaccine-induced immunity, and species differentiation. This review summarizes current knowledge regarding the structure, biological functions, and diagnostic and vaccine potential of major orthopoxvirus recombinant antigens. Particular attention is given to the genomic organization of Orthopoxvirus, differences between intracellular mature virion (IMV) and extracellular enveloped virion (EV) forms, and the characteristics of key antigens, including A29, M1, H3, A35, and B6. Comparative phylogenetic analyses demonstrated a high degree of conservation among structurally important orthopoxvirus proteins while also identifying variable regions potentially relevant for differential diagnostics. Available evidence indicates that IMV-associated proteins are primarily involved in virus neutralization, whereas EV-associated antigens contribute mainly to limiting viral dissemination. Consequently, multicomponent antigen strategies combining IMV- and EV-associated proteins appear to provide the greatest potential for the development of effective serological assays and next-generation subunit vaccines. Overall, rational antigen selection should be based on integrated evaluation of structural, functional, and immunological properties to optimize orthopoxvirus diagnostic and vaccine platforms.

analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on the selection of recombinant orthopoxvirus proteins for immunobiological and diagnostic applications, specifically addressing the Mpox virus and its clades. The central question is how to optimize the use of these proteins in developing effective diagnostic tools and vaccines.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is based on comparative phylogenetic analyses and integrates structural, functional, and immunological properties of key orthopoxvirus proteins. It does not explicitly report on databases, search dates, or meta-analysis methods.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that multicomponent antigen strategies combining IMV- and EV-associated proteins offer the greatest potential for effective serological assays and subunit vaccines. It highlights the importance of integrating structural, functional, and immunological properties for rational antigen selection.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that while there is a high degree of conservation among structurally important orthopoxvirus proteins, there are variable regions that may be relevant for differential diagnostics. However, the evidence does not provide detailed information on the specific mechanisms or implications of these variable regions.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that future research should focus on the development of multicomponent antigen strategies and the integration of structural, functional, and immunological data to optimize diagnostic and vaccine platforms for Mpox virus.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the selection of recombinant orthopoxvirus proteins for immunobiological and diagnostic applications, emphasizing the importance of understanding the structural, functional, and immunological properties of key antigens such as A29, M1, H3, A35, and B6. It highlights the high antigenic similarity among orthopoxviruses, which complicates serological diagnostics but also supports cross-reactive immune responses. The review concludes that combining IMV- and EV-associated proteins in multicomponent strategies could enhance the effectiveness of serological assays and subunit vaccines. However, the evidence does not fully address the mechanisms or implications of variable regions identified in phylogenetic analyses. The study underscores the need for further research to refine antigen selection and improve diagnostic and vaccine platforms for Mpox virus.

papers.abstract_zh: 正如最近的全球 猴痘 暴发 所强调的那样,正痘病毒 是人畜共患 DNA 病毒,对公共卫生具有持续重要性。正痘病毒 之间的高抗原相似性使得 免疫应答 能够发生交叉反应,但使用于血清监测、评估既往暴露、评估 疫苗 诱导的免疫和物种分化的血清学诊断系统的开发变得复杂。本综述总结了有关主要 正痘病毒 重组抗原的结构、生物学功能以及诊断和 疫苗 潜力的当前知识。特别关注 正痘病毒 的基因组组织、细胞内成熟病毒颗粒 (IMV) 和细胞外有包膜病毒颗粒 (EV) 形式之间的差异,以及关键抗原的特征,包括 A29、M1、H3、A35 和 B6。比较系统发育分析表明,结构重要的 正痘病毒 蛋白之间具有高度保守性,同时还鉴定了可能与鉴别诊断相关的可变区域。现有证据表明,IMV 相关蛋白主要参与病毒中和,而 EV 相关抗原主要有助于限制病毒传播。因此,结合 IMV 和 EV 相关蛋白的多组分抗原策略似乎为开发有效的血清学检测和下一代亚基 疫苗 提供了最大的潜力。总体而言,合理的抗原选择应基于结构、功能和免疫学特性的综合评估,以优化正痘病毒诊断和疫苗平台。

papers.title: Dynamics of Orthopoxvirus Stability Under Simulated Luminal Conditions of the Gastrointestinal Tract for Assessing the Feasibility of Oral Immunization
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Mpox (formerly monkeypox) is a re-emerging global health threat. While current vaccines are injectable, oral vaccination offers a painless alternative, though the harsh gastrointestinal (GI) environment challenges live viral vaccines. This study evaluated the stability of orthopoxviruses under simulated GI conditions to assess the physicochemical feasibility of oral mpox immunization. Methods: Attenuated and virulent strains of vaccinia, cowpox, and camelpox viruses were exposed to simulated gastric (pH 1.0–2.0 and 3.0–4.0 with pepsin) and intestinal (pH 7.0–7.5) conditions at 37 °C for 180 min. Viral titers were determined via cell culture assays. The physicochemical protective efficacy of enteric-coated capsules was evaluated using standard dissolution testing parameters. Results: All orthopoxviruses were rapidly inactivated under highly acidic fasting conditions (pH 1.0–2.0). However, they exhibited high stability at pH 3.0–4.0 and 7.0–7.5, retaining approximately 20–30% of their initial infectivity after 180 min. Enteric-coated capsules successfully maintained shell integrity in simulated gastric fluids for over 3 h and dissolved completely under intestinal conditions within ~130 min, aligning with small intestine transit times. Conclusions: Orthopoxviruses possess sufficient intestinal stability to support the physicochemical feasibility of oral immunization, provided they are protected from gastric acidity. Enteric-coated capsules represent a highly suitable delivery system for the intestinal release of live orthopoxvirus-based candidates, warranting further in vivo preclinical evaluation.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景/目标:猴痘(以前称为猴痘)是一种重新出现的全球健康威胁。虽然目前的 疫苗 是可注射的,但口服 疫苗 提供了一种无痛替代方案,尽管恶劣的胃肠 (GI) 环境对活病毒 疫苗 提出了挑战。本研究评估了 正痘病毒 在模拟胃肠道条件下的稳定性,以评估口服 猴痘 免疫的理化可行性。方法:将牛痘、牛痘和骆驼痘病毒的减毒毒株暴露于 37°C 的模拟胃(pH 1.0-2.0 和 3.0-4.0,胃蛋白酶)和肠道(pH 7.0-7.5)条件下 180 分钟。通过细胞培养测定确定病毒滴度。使用标准溶出测试参数评估肠溶胶囊的理化保护功效。结果:所有 正痘病毒 在高酸性禁食条件下(pH 1.0-2.0)迅速失活。然而,它们在 pH 3.0-4.0 和 7.0-7.5 下表现出高度稳定性,180 分钟后保留了约 20-30% 的初始感染性。肠溶胶囊在模拟胃液中成功保持壳完整性超过 3 小时,并在肠道条件下在约 130 分钟内完全溶解,与小肠转运时间一致。结论:正痘病毒 具有足够的肠道稳定性,以支持口服免疫的理化可行性,前提是它们免受胃酸的影响。肠溶胶囊代表了一种非常适合肠道释放活体 正痘病毒 候选药物的递送系统,值得进一步的体内临床前评估。

analysis_zh.main_results: 所有 正痘病毒 在高酸性禁食条件下(pH 1.0-2.0)均迅速失活,但在 pH 3.0-4.0 和 7.0-7.5 下表现出高稳定性,180 分钟后保留了约 20-30% 的初始感染性。肠溶胶囊在模拟胃液中成功保持壳完整性超过 3 小时,并在肠道条件下在约 130 分钟内完全溶解。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者得出的结论是,正痘病毒 具有足够的肠道稳定性,以支持口服免疫的理化可行性,前提是它们免受胃酸的影响。肠溶胶囊被认为是非常适合基于 正痘病毒 的活体 疫苗 的递送系统。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,通过适当的保护措施,针对 猴痘 的口服免疫是可行的,这可能会导致非侵入性 疫苗 递送系统的开发。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是在模拟条件下进行的,没有考虑体内的复杂性,这可能会影响结果的普遍性。由于数据仅具有抽象性质,证据的强度中等。

Mediar Therapeutics Enters Antibody Collaboration with Ono Pharma for Fibro-Inflammatory Diseases ByEmily Schoenthaler August 6th 2026 Mediar Therapeutics has signed a collaboration and option agreement with Ono Pharmaceutical to co-develop novel antibody therapeutics targeting myofibroblast biology in fibro-inflammatory diseases, building on Mediar's existing three-program antifibrotic antibody pipeline. FDA Accepts Merck's Application to Expand Enflonsia into Second RSV Season ByFeliza Mirasol August 6th 2026 Backed by an 84.3% drop in RSV hospitalizations, Enflonsia could extend protection to high-risk infants still vulnerable in their second season. Sanofi Pauses Phase 2 Trial of Monoclonal Antibody SAR445399 in Chronic Lung Disease ByEmily Schoenthaler August 6th 2026 Sanofi has suspended a phase 2 trial of SAR445399, an anti-IL-1R3 monoclonal antibody, in non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis, part of new ceo Belén Garijo's ongoing portfolio review rather than a safety concern. Moderna's mFLUSIVA Approval Validates mRNA Platform Beyond COVID-19: What It Means for Biopharmaceutical Manufacturing ByBioPharm International Staff August 6th 2026 The FDA's approval of mFLUSIVA (mRNA-1010) extends Moderna's lipid nanoparticle platform to a new indication, with broad implications for biopharmaceutical manufacturing flexibility and regulatory precedent. Advertisement The BioPharm Brief: Platforms, Precision, and Patient Access ByEmily Schoenthaler Published: August 5th 2026 | Updated: July 30th 2026 Today’s BioPharm Brief highlights new advances in engineered tissues, regenerative medicine, and biologics delivery, including clinical progress for a tissue-engineered therapy, late-stage wound healing data, and a major subcutaneous delivery licensing deal. Applied Biologics Gains IRB Approval for Phase 3 BIOxHEAL Trial in Diabetic Foot Ulcers ByFeliza Mirasol August 5th 2026 Nonhealing wounds precede 80% of diabetes-related amputations, and BIOxHEAL is now cleared to test whether it can change that in a controlled trial. Alteogen Licenses Subcutaneous Platform to Undisclosed Global Pharma Company in Deal Worth Up to $365 Million ByFeliza Mirasol August 5th 2026 Alteogen has licensed its ALT-B4 subcutaneous platform to an undisclosed global pharmaceutical company in a deal worth up to $365 million. Satellite Bio Wins FDA IND Clearance for SB-101, Marking Transition to Clinical-Stage Company ByEmily Schoenthaler August 5th 2026 The FDA has cleared Satellite Bio's IND application for SB-101, an off-the-shelf hepatocyte cell therapy for urea cycle disorders, marking the company's transition to clinical-stage status ahead of a planned Phase 1/2 trial in infants later this year. Kyverna Therapeutics and ElevateBio Sign Commercial Manufacturing Agreement for Miv-Cel ByEmily Schoenthaler August 5th 2026 Kyverna Therapeutics and ElevateBio have entered a commercial manufacturing and supply agreement for miv-cel, Kyverna's autologous CD19-targeting CAR T-cell therapy, securing scalable production ahead of a planned launch in stiff person syndrome. analysis.brief_en: Bavarian Nordic has secured EU approval to expand its mpox/smallpox vaccine to children aged 2 years and older, marking a significant development in public health preparedness. This decision follows the company's efforts to broaden the vaccine's application, which could enhance protection against mpox outbreaks in younger populations. The approval is based on the vaccine's existing efficacy and safety profiles, though further studies may be required to confirm its suitability for children. The event is confirmed by the EU's regulatory action, and the response status is under investigation to assess the broader implications of this expansion. No specific case counts, death counts, or exposure numbers are reported in the evidence, but the move is expected to increase the vaccine's public health impact. The approval reflects a proactive approach to addressing mpox risks, particularly in communities where the virus has shown increased transmission potential.

news.title_zh: Bavarian Nordic 获得欧盟批准将 猴痘/Smalpox 疫苗 扩大到 2 岁儿童 - BioPharm International
news.source_body_en: Bavarian Nordic has secured EU approval to expand its mpox/smallpox vaccine to children aged 2 years and older, marking a significant development in public health preparedness. This decision follows the company's efforts to broaden the vaccine's application, which could enhance protection against mpox outbreaks in younger populations. The approval is based on the vaccine's existing efficacy and safety profiles, though further studies may be required to confirm its suitability for children. The event is confirmed by the EU's regulatory action, and the response status is under investigation to assess the broader implications of this expansion. No specific case counts, death counts, or exposure numbers are reported in the evidence, but the move is expected to increase the vaccine's public health impact. The approval reflects a proactive approach to addressing mpox risks, particularly in communities where the virus has shown increased transmission potential.
news.content_zh: Bavarian Nordic 已获得欧盟批准,将其 猴痘/天花 疫苗 扩大到 2 岁及以上儿童,这标志着公共卫生准备工作取得了重大进展。这一决定是在该公司努力扩大 疫苗 的应用范围之后做出的,这可以增强对年轻人群体的 猴痘 暴发 的保护。此次批准是基于 疫苗 现有的功效和安全性概况,但可能需要进一步研究来确认其是否适合儿童。该事件已得到欧盟监管行动的证实,目前正在调查响应状态,以评估此次扩张的更广泛影响。证据中没有报告具体的病例数、死亡数或暴露数量,但此举预计将增加 疫苗 对公共卫生的影响。此次批准反映了解决 猴痘 风险的积极主动方法,特别是在病毒已显示出 猴痘 潜力增加的社区。

news.content: 26°C broken clouds TFL Updates Search for: Search Search LDN Write For Us Login London News Lifestyle Entrepreneurship Fitness & Health Finance Tech Food & Drink Automotive Travel Global UKHSA overview: 119 mpox clade Ib cases in UK to 31 July 2026, majority of England cases in London By LDN Editor 08 August 2026 3 minute read Listen to this article UKHSA overview: 119 mpox clade Ib cases in UK to 31 July 2026, majority of England cases in London The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) epidemiological overview for 6 August 2026 reports 119 cases of mpox clade Ib in the UK recorded up to 31 July 2026, with most of the England cases reported in London. The same report sets out recent genomic findings, transmission notes and vaccination figures for England to the end of March 2026. Cases at a glance Total mpox clade Ib cases in the UK to 31 July 2026: 119; Distribution of clade Ib cases: 82 in England (the majority in London), 24 in Northern Ireland, 7 in Scotland and 6 in Wales; Separately, between 2023 and 31 July 2026 a total of 1,035 mpox clade IIb cases were reported in the UK: 968 in England, 9 in Northern Ireland, 37 in Scotland and 21 in Wales. Vaccination data for England (to 31 March 2026) The UKHSA overview provides vaccination figures for England up to 31 March 2026. In that period 101,210 first doses and 63,915 second doses of mpox vaccine were administered across England. London accounted for the largest number of first doses, with 63,624 first doses delivered in the capital; the London total for second doses recorded in the report is 42,902. Recent virus and transmission findings The report records that in December 2025 genomic surveillance identified a recombinant mpox virus in England in an individual who had recently travelled to Asia. Sequencing showed the mpox genome in that case contained elements of both clade Ib and clade IIb. The overview also notes that from October 2025 community transmission through gay, bisexual, and other men who have sex with men (GBMSM) networks was reported in Europe and North America. The UKHSA report presents these items as part of its epidemiological summary. Vaccination policy and local offers The report states that the reactive vaccination offer ended nationally in summer 2023. It also records that the reactive offer continued to be provided in London and in Greater Manchester in response to ongoing local transmission and identification of mpox case clusters. What the report does and does not say The UKHSA overview sets out confirmed case counts, the geographic breakdowns above, vaccination totals for England to 31 March 2026 and the sequencing finding from December 2025. The report indicates that most of the 82 clade Ib cases recorded in England were reported in London and that London received the largest share of first doses administered in England. The document does not use the term “epicentre” to describe London, and it does not provide an explicit explanation of the causes of the geographic distribution of cases or of why vaccine delivery was concentrated in particular areas. Causal interpretations of the figures are not provided in the overview and are not confirmed by the report. Practical implications in the report The overview combines case counts, regional breakdowns, vaccination uptake figures and genomic findings in a single epidemiological summary. Readers are advised that the figures cited cover different cut-off dates in the report: cases are recorded to 31 July 2026 for the clade Ib and IIb counts, while the vaccination totals are reported to 31 March 2026. Where the report gives precise numbers or dates these have been used above. Where the report does not provide explanatory or causal statements about the geographic distribution or programme delivery, those elements have not been inferred. The full details are available in the published information. For related coverage, read England and Wales face historic drought following driest July on record. news.content: ALTAMONTE SPRINGS, FLORIDA - DECEMBER 16: Vials of smallpox vaccine sit on a counter before a vaccination December 16, 2002 at Mid-Florida Biologicals in Altamonte Springs, Florida. The health center is part of a 16-clinic trial study looking at smallpox vaccinations. According to Dr. Ronald Brown of Mid-Florida Biologicals,, there have been no reports of adverse side effects due to the vaccine among the 2,500 local participants in the study . Chris Livingston/Getty Images The European Commission granted marketing authorization for Bavarian Nordic's IMVANEX mpox and smallpox vaccine to cover children aged 2 to under 12 years — the first time any major regulatory authority has formally cleared a non-replicating mpox vaccine for this age group — closing a gap that left toddlers and school-age children in Africa's worst-hit countries without a formally authorized shot as they bore more than half of the continent's mpox deaths. Children under 15 represent roughly 60 percent of confirmed mpox cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo and approximately 80 percent of recorded deaths — making them the primary victims of an outbreak that has never been primarily a disease of adults in the DRC. This was confirmed by UNICEF data from 2024 . The decision, formally adopted by the Commission on August 7, 2026, converts a positive recommendation issued by the European Medicines Agency's Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use on June 25, 2026 into a legally binding EU-wide marketing authorization covering all member states and the European Economic Area. The vaccine — known internationally as JYNNEOS in the United States, IMVAMUNE in Canada, and IMVANEX in the EU, the United Kingdom, and the EEA — is now authorized in the EU for everyone aged two and older, as confirmed in Bavarian Nordic's official announcement . Why Children Could Not Get This Vaccine Before The EU gap was structural. IMVANEX received its original EU marketing authorization in 2013 for adults and was extended to adolescents in 2024 to cover ages 12 to 17. That sequential age expansion followed an NIH-sponsored study in adolescents; the 2-to-11 age group required a separate trial, in part because regulators cannot ethically extrapolate pediatric data from adult studies and in part because the populations most affected — DRC children, many of them malnourished or HIV-exposed — live in countries far removed from the trial sites where prior adult and adolescent data were collected. The regulatory gap had real consequences. When 265,000 doses of MVA-BN arrived in the DRC in September 2024 and vaccination began in October of that year, health authorities directed those shots primarily to adults. The children accounting for 80 percent of deaths were not the primary targets of that campaign — because the vaccine had no authorized indication for children, and national regulatory agencies and multilateral bodies follow stringent-regulator clearances when making formal deployment decisions. This is confirmed by UNICEF reporting on DRC vaccination . What the DRC and Uganda Trial Showed The regulatory bridge was a Phase 2 clinical study, NCT06549530, sponsored by Bavarian Nordic and co-funded by the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations with a $6.5 million award . The trial enrolled 227 children aged 2 to under 12 years and 224 adults aged 18 to 50 at sites in the DRC and Uganda — both countries experiencing active mpox transmission — which means the immunogenicity data was generated in the precise populations that stand to benefit from the authorization. Each participant received two standard-dose injections four weeks apart. Topline results, announced in October 2025, showed that the immune response in children two weeks after the second dose was non-inferior to that in adults — meaning the vaccine produced at least as strong a response in children as it did in the comparator group. Across the full pediatric cohort, immune responses were 2.5 times greater than in the adult group, with the highest responses observed in the youngest subgroup of children aged 2 to 5. Bavarian Nordic submitted the data to the EMA on March 27, 2026, as confirmed in the EMA submission announcement , and the CHMP adopted its positive opinion at its June 22–25, 2026 meeting. The safety profile in children was comparable to that in adults, with no unexpected adverse events. The World Health Organization's Global Advisory Committee on Vaccine Safety, which reviewed MVA-BN safety data including in special populations through its May 2025 report, found no safety concerns identified in children, HIV-positive individuals, or other vulnerable groups assessed, though it noted that some subgroup sample sizes were small. Why Non-Replication Is the Critical Technical Detail Most discussion of IMVANEX treats it simply as "the mpox vaccine." The technical distinction that makes it irreplaceable for DRC children is not often explained: MVA-BN cannot replicate inside human cells. To understand why that matters, consider how the vaccine was made. MVA (Modified Vaccinia Ankara) was derived from vaccinia virus — the same viral family used in traditional smallpox vaccination — by serial passage more than 500 times through chicken embryo fibroblast cells in Munich between 1953 and 1968. That process caused the virus to accumulate approximately six major deletions in its genome, together accounting for roughly 10 percent of its ancestral genetic information. Among the genes lost were those that allow vaccinia to complete its replication cycle in most mammalian cells. Today, MVA-BN can enter human cells and express its genes — triggering the immune response that provides protection against mpox and smallpox — but the replication cycle is blocked at the virion assembly stage: immature particles form inside cells but cannot be released to spread infection. That single biological constraint has major clinical significance for the children at the center of the DRC outbreak. First-generation replicating smallpox vaccines such as ACAM2000 and Dryvax are contraindicated in immunocompromised individuals because a live-replicating vaccinia virus can cause serious disease in people whose immune systems cannot control it. Malnutrition-related immunosuppression and HIV — both common in the DRC and among mpox-affected children in the region — fall squarely into that contraindication. MVA-BN does not carry this risk, because replication cannot proceed. It is the only authorized mpox vaccine that can be safely administered to immunocompromised children. There is a tradeoff. Because MVA-BN does not replicate, the peak neutralizing antibody titers it induces are roughly 10 to 20 times lower than those produced by replicating vaccines, and those titers wane within six months toward baseline after the two-dose course. Memory B cells remain detectable at one year, and T-cell responses are more durable, but the full immunological correlate of protection against mpox has not been established. The clinical relevance of the antibody waning question remains uncertain. What the NCT06549530 data do confirm is that the immune response across the full pediatric cohort substantially exceeded the adult response — suggesting that children may mount a more robust reaction than the two-dose schedule was designed around in adults. From Brussels to Kinshasa: What the Authorization Does Not Solve EU regulatory clearance carries real weight beyond European borders. EMA assessments serve as the template for WHO prequalification, which in turn enables United Nations agencies and multilateral procurement bodies to purchase and distribute the vaccine in countries lacking the regulatory infrastructure for independent review. The original WHO prequalification of MVA-BN — granted September 13, 2024, for adults — was built on EMA's prior adult authorization, and the DRC's own emergency use approval referenced the EMA and FDA decisions. The 2026 pediatric extension will follow the same pattern: a fresh WHO prequalification covering children aged 2 to under 12 is expected, which will give international procurement bodies formal authority to direct doses specifically to children. But formal authorization is not the same as delivered doses. As of May 2025, a WHO committee reviewing vaccination progress noted that over 651,000 doses of MVA-BN had been administered on the African continent, with 96 percent of those doses going to the DRC. That figure reflects the scale of the challenge: a continent with over a billion people saw fewer than 700,000 total doses reach outbreak-affected populations, and even that limited supply faced significant cold chain and logistics hurdles. The DRC's vast geography and weak infrastructure in conflict-affected provinces mean that reaching children — who may live in internally displaced persons camps in North Kivu or in communities with no functional cold chain equipment — requires a different kind of delivery architecture than an EU-style vaccination campaign. Independent research has documented the specific bottlenecks in mpox vaccine access : cold chain limitations, shortages of trained healthcare workers, inadequate last-mile distribution networks, and underresourced national procurement mechanisms. These barriers do not disappear when a regulatory document is signed in Brussels. Bavarian Nordic and CEPI, whose partnership has also launched separate trials covering infants under two and pregnant women, have acknowledged the gap between authorization and access. CEPI's Mpox Programme Lead Kristine Rose has publicly emphasized that vaccines can only protect lives if they reach those who need them, and that children have too often been among the last to benefit from vaccine development. The EC approval announced August 7 addresses the regulatory barrier; the operational barriers remain . IMVANEX After August 7 With this authorization, MVA-BN now carries formal EU approval across the full post-infancy age range — from two years through adulthood — for active immunization against mpox, smallpox, and vaccinia virus disease. The EU authorization runs across 27 member states plus the broader EEA, and the UK authorization mirrors EU decisions for IMVANEX independently. The EMA originally cleared IMVANEX in 2013 under "exceptional circumstances" — a regulatory pathway used when comprehensive efficacy data cannot be generated under normal conditions, which in this case reflects the eradication of smallpox and the difficulty of conducting controlled mpox efficacy trials in endemic settings. The exceptional-circumstances designation means the product remains under additional monitoring even after each age-group extension, with ongoing safety data requirements. The August 7 decision extends that framework to children aged 2 to under 12. Bavarian Nordic is simultaneously conducting a separate clinical trial program for infants under two years of age and for pregnant and breastfeeding women, launched June 2025 in DRC with CEPI co-funding. Those trials are expected to produce data that could support a further label expansion for the youngest children and for pregnant populations — the remaining vulnerable groups without formal EU authorization. The path from trial initiation to regulatory decision for those populations is likely to take several more years. Frequently Asked Questions Can children in the United States now get the IMVANEX mpox vaccine? No — this is a European Union authorization only. In the United States, the equivalent vaccine (sold as JYNNEOS) is approved by the FDA for adults 18 and older. The FDA granted an emergency use authorization for adolescents during the 2022 mpox outbreak but has not extended a full authorization to children under 18. The EU decision creates pressure and a scientific evidence base that could support an FDA pediatric submission, but US clearance would require a separate regulatory process. Parents of young children in the US who are concerned about mpox exposure should discuss options with their pediatrician. Why are young children in Africa so much more at risk from mpox than children in Europe or the United States? Several compounding factors increase pediatric severity and mortality in the DRC specifically. The current dominant strain — mpox Clade Ib — is associated with higher virulence and easier human-to-human transmission than the Clade IIb strain that drove the 2022 global outbreak in adults. Children in outbreak-affected DRC regions often have malnutrition-related immunosuppression or HIV exposure, both of which impair the immune response to the virus. Cross-protective immunity from the smallpox vaccination campaign that ended in 1980 is absent in everyone born after that period, leaving all children — and most adults under 46 — with no background orthopoxvirus immunity. These factors together produce an infant mortality rate among children under one year that is fourfold higher than among those over 15. Will the EU approval mean children in the DRC can now get the vaccine? Not automatically. EU authorization does not govern procurement or deployment in African countries. What it does enable is a fresh WHO prequalification for the pediatric indication, which allows UN agencies and multilateral procurement bodies to formally purchase doses for children — a step that was not possible when the vaccine was adult-only. But even with WHO prequalification, the bottlenecks that limited the first 651,000 adult doses to 96 percent DRC coverage remain: cold chain infrastructure, last-mile logistics in conflict zones, trained health workers, and funding. Those operational barriers require investment and coordination that goes beyond what a regulatory decision can provide. What is the difference between the mpox vaccine IMVANEX and older smallpox vaccines? IMVANEX (MVA-BN) is a third-generation, non-replicating vaccine. It can enter human cells and trigger an immune response, but a block in the viral lifecycle at the assembly stage prevents it from producing infectious particles that spread within or between people. Older smallpox vaccines like ACAM2000 use live, replicating vaccinia virus, which produces stronger and more durable antibody responses but cannot be safely used in immunocompromised individuals — including children with HIV or severe malnutrition. For the DRC pediatric population, MVA-BN is the only authorized option precisely because it does not carry the replication risk

Kenya News Agency - KNA's Post Kenya News Agency - KNA 4d · The County Government of Nakuru has rolled out a massive vaccination exercise against the monkeypox (Mpox) virus. For the next three weeks, the vaccine would be administered in a phased approach in Maai Mahiu, Longonot and Salgaa areas, targeting high-risk groups. According to County Executive Committee Member (CECM) for Health services Ms Roselyn Mungai, the exercise will focus on those at highest risk, including people who have had close physical contact with confirmed cases, populations at increased risk such as long-distance truck drivers and sex workers and healthcare workers who provide direct care to Mpox patients. Ms Mungai assured members of the public that the vaccine, which has been shown to be up to 82 percent effective in reducing disease severity, transmission and mortality, was safe. The CECM said the roll-out is an important milestone and will serve as an additional public health measure to complement a comprehensive response to the Mpox outbreak as well as other measures already in place.. The vaccination programme is being implemented through the collaborative efforts of the Sub-County Health Management Teams, Sub-County AIDS and STI Coordinators (SCASCOs) and healthcare workers, who are not only administering vaccines but also educating communities on Mpox prevention and the importance of seeking care early. “Under the leadership of Governor Susan Kihika, Nakuru County continues to strengthen disease surveillance, outbreak preparedness and preventive healthcare, while encouraging all eligible residents in the targeted areas to receive the Mpox vaccine at the designated vaccination sites,” stated the CECM. She added, "The Mpox vaccination campaign will not target the general population but will prioritize high-risk groups. This vaccine is not a silver bullet but one of several public health measures being used as part of a comprehensive response to the outbreak. It complements our broader efforts to contain and manage mpox in Kenya." In addition to vaccination and screening efforts, the County Government’s Department of Health is conducting laboratory tests to identify and isolate new cases and conducting regular contact tracing. “The campaign will prioritize truck drivers, cross-border PSV drivers and sex workers, with vaccination offered at fixed wellness centers strategically located at truck stopovers in Mai Mahiu and Salgaa along the Northern Transport Corridor,” disclosed Ms Mungai. The CECM said the initiative is designed to protect the most vulnerable groups who are at increased risk of exposure due to the nature of their work and mobility. Mpox was first confirmed in Kenya in 2023, with sporadic cases occurring throughout the year. However, the situation has deteriorated in recent months, requiring a more urgent and coordinated response. All reactions: 2 1 share Like Comment All reactions: 2 1 share Like Comment

news.source_body_en: The County Government of Nakuru has initiated a three-week vaccination campaign against the monkeypox (Mpox) virus, targeting high-risk groups in Maai Mahiu, Longonot, and Salgaa. The program, led by County Executive Committee Member Ms Roselyn Mungai, focuses on individuals with close contact with confirmed cases, long-distance truck drivers, sex workers, and healthcare workers. The vaccine is reported to be up to 82% effective in reducing disease severity, transmission, and mortality. The initiative is part of a broader public health response, complementing existing measures to contain the Mpox outbreak. Vaccination sites are strategically located at truck stopovers in the targeted areas, and the Department of Health is conducting laboratory tests, contact tracing, and isolation of new cases. The campaign emphasizes protecting vulnerable populations due to their increased exposure risk. The vaccination effort is described as a milestone in the county's disease surveillance and outbreak preparedness strategy.

Bavarian Nordic Receives European Commission Approval of Mpox/Smallpox Vaccine for Children Aged 2 to Less than 12 Years Bavarian Nordic A/S Fri, August 7, 2026 at 1:00 AM CDT 3 min read BAVA.CO +0.80% Bavarian Nordic A/S MVA-BN approval expanded to include children aged 2 to less than 12 years for protection against mpox, smallpox and disease caused by vaccinia virus Approval further strengthens MVA-BN's position in supporting global public health preparedness COPENHAGEN, Denmark, August 7, 2026 – Bavarian Nordic A/S (OMX: BAVA) announced today that the European Commission has adopted the recent Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use (CHMP) positive opinion recommending the approval of a type II variation for IMVANEX® (MVA-BN) smallpox and mpox vaccine, extending the current marketing authorization to include children 2 to less than 12 years of age. The approval is based on data from a Phase 2 clinical study (NCT06549530) involving 227 children aged 2 to <12 years and 224 adults, demonstrating non-inferior immune responses and a similar safety profile in children compared to adults following vaccination with two standard doses of MVA-BN. The study was co-funded by the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI). With this approval, MVA-BN is now authorized in the European Union for use in individuals aged 2 years and older, marking a significant expansion of access to a non-replicating vaccine designed to help protect vulnerable populations against mpox, smallpox and disease caused by vaccinia virus. Paul Chaplin, President and Chief Executive Officer of Bavarian Nordic, said: "The European Commission's approval of MVA-BN for children aged 2 to less than 12 years represents an important advancement in our efforts to broaden access to protection against mpox and smallpox. Children have carried a disproportionate burden during recent mpox outbreaks, particularly in parts of Africa, underscoring the importance of making safe and effective vaccines available to this vulnerable population. We are grateful to the study participants, investigators, CEPI and our partners whose collaboration helped generate the data supporting this approval." The approval adds to the growing body of clinical evidence supporting the use of MVA-BN across age groups and further strengthens Bavarian Nordic's commitment to supporting global public health preparedness and outbreak response. About the mpox and smallpox vaccine MVA-BN or Modified Vaccinia Ankara-Bavarian Nordic is the only non-replicating mpox vaccine approved in the U.S., Switzerland, Singapore, Mexico (marketed as JYNNEOS®), Canada (marketed as IMVAMUNE®), the EU/EEA European Economic Area and United Kingdom (marketed as IMVANEX®). Originally developed as a smallpox vaccine in collaboration with the U.S. government to ensure the supply of a smallpox vaccine for the entire population, including immunocompromised individuals who are not recommended vaccination with traditional replicating smallpox vaccines, MVA-BN has been indicated for use in the general population (from 2 years old) in individuals considered at risk for smallpox or mpox infection. Story Continues About Bavarian Nordic Bavarian Nordic is a global vaccine company with a mission to improve health and save lives through innovative vaccines. We are a preferred supplier of mpox and smallpox vaccines to governments to enhance public health preparedness and have a leading portfolio of travel vaccines. Bavarian Nordic Receives European Commission Approval of Mpox/Smallpox Vaccine for Children Aged 2 to Less than 12 Years Bavarian Nordic A/S Fri, August 7, 2026 at 1:00 AM CDT 3 min read BAVA.CO +0.80% Bavarian Nordic A/S MVA-BN approval expanded to include children aged 2 to less than 12 years for protection against mpox, smallpox and disease caused by vaccinia virus Approval further strengthens MVA-BN's position in supporting global public health preparedness COPENHAGEN, Denmark, August 7, 2026 – Bavarian Nordic A/S (OMX: BAVA) announced today that the European Commission has adopted the recent Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use (CHMP) positive opinion recommending the approval of a type II variation for IMVANEX® (MVA-BN) smallpox and mpox vaccine, extending the current marketing authorization to include children 2 to less than 12 years of age. The approval is based on data from a Phase 2 clinical study (NCT06549530) involving 227 children aged 2 to <12 years and 224 adults, demonstrating non-inferior immune responses and a similar safety profile in children compared to adults following vaccination with two standard doses of MVA-BN. The study was co-funded by the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI). With this approval, MVA-BN is now authorized in the European Union for use in individuals aged 2 years and older, marking a significant expansion of access to a non-replicating vaccine designed to help protect vulnerable populations against mpox, smallpox and disease caused by vaccinia virus. Paul Chaplin, President and Chief Executive Officer of Bavarian Nordic, said: "The European Commission's approval of MVA-BN for children aged 2 to less than 12 years represents an important advancement in our efforts to broaden access to protection against mpox and smallpox. Children have carried a disproportionate burden during recent mpox outbreaks, particularly in parts of Africa, underscoring the importance of making safe and effective vaccines available to this vulnerable population. We are grateful to the study participants, investigators, CEPI and our partners whose collaboration helped generate the data supporting this approval." The approval adds to the growing body of clinical evidence supporting the use of MVA-BN across age groups and further strengthens Bavarian Nordic's commitment to supporting global public health preparedness and outbreak response. About the mpox and smallpox vaccine MVA-BN or Modified Vaccinia Ankara-Bavarian Nordic is the only non-replicating mpox vaccine approved in the U.S., Switzerland, Singapore, Mexico (marketed as JYNNEOS®), Canada (marketed as IMVAMUNE®), the EU/EEA European Economic Area and United Kingdom (marketed as IMVANEX®). Originally developed as a smallpox vaccine in collaboration with the U.S. government to ensure the supply of a smallpox vaccine for the entire population, including immunocompromised individuals who are not recommended vaccination with traditional replicating smallpox vaccines, MVA-BN has been indicated for use in the general population (from 2 years old) in individuals considered at risk for smallpox or mpox infection. WHO: Mpox Is Not the New COVID, But We Must Act Now Camilla Jessen • August 20, 2024 Follow dagens.com on Google Photo: Wikimedia Commons Mpox is not the new COVID-19. Others are reading now Woman reports Type 2 diabetes remission after changing diet and losing weight Prince versus voters in tiny nation’s abortion fight A World Health Organization (WHO) representative stressed on Tuesday that mpox, in either its new or old strain, is not the next COVID-19, as authorities are well-equipped to control its spread. “We can and must fight mpox together,” said Hans Kluge, WHO Regional Director for Europe, during a UN media briefing, according to Reuters. “So, will we choose to put the systems in place to control and eliminate mpox worldwide? Or will we enter another cycle of panic and neglect? How we respond now and in the years to come will be a crucial test for Europe and the world,” he added. Also read As fallen soldiers return home, a collapsed peace deal pushes the US and Iran back to the brink of all-out war Trump takes dramatic step after 90-minute call with Putin Mpox, a viral infection causing pus-filled lesions and flu-like symptoms, is typically mild but can be fatal. The Clade 1b variant has raised global concerns due to its seemingly easier transmission through close contact. Last week, Sweden confirmed its first case of the Clade 1b variant, linked to a growing outbreak in Africa—the first instance of its spread outside the continent. Following the identification of this new variant, the WHO declared the outbreak a public health emergency of international concern. Kluge emphasized that focusing on the new Clade 1 strain will also strengthen efforts against the less severe Clade 2 variant, which has been spreading globally since 2022. This approach will enhance Europe’s response through improved health guidance and monitoring. Approximately 100 new cases of the Clade 2 Mpox strain are now being reported monthly in the European region, Kluge noted. Mpox is primarily transmitted through close physical contact, including sexual contact. However, unlike previous global pandemics such as COVID-19, there is no evidence that it spreads easily through the air. news.content_title: Fears contagious mpox strain that causes painful blister rash silently spreading in UK amid ‘rapid’ outbreak
news.content: EXPERTS have sounded the alarm over a concerning rise in mpox cases in the UK. Scientists today told Sun Health that the “continued detection” of cases suggest the virus is spreading silently” . A report published last week by health officials in Northern Ireland confirmed it was aware of a “rapidly developing outbreak” in the country Credit: Alamy Latest figures suggest that there have been at least 100 cases of the clade 1b mutation in the UK so far this year, the majority in London. By comparison, just 21 cases were logged across the entirety of 2025, according to the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA). Sign up for the Health newsletter Thank you! A report published last week by health officials in Northern Ireland also confirmed it was aware of a “rapidly developing outbreak” in the country, accounting for at least 22 cases in June. Most of the cases had no travel abroad in recent weeks, suggesting spread in the community. Anyone eligible for the mpox vaccine in the UK has been urged to get it, to thwart any potential spread of the virus across the country. A different, less severe, form of mpox, called clade 2, sparked alarm in 2022, when it spread globally, mainly through sexual contact among gay and bisexual men. However, new infections gradually tapered off amid boosted awareness of the disease and a hurried vaccination program. At the time the UK reported almost 4,000 cases, with NHS England inoculating over 68,000 people against the disease with the smallpox vaccine, which works due to the two viruses being closely related. According to the new report from the Public Health Agency in Belfast , all cases were men with an average age of 41. Six had reported previously having at least one dose of the vaccine, with 12 confirming they had not had a vaccine. Five of the patients required hospital treatment. Writing in the journal Eurosurveillance , the scientists said: “ Before June 2026, there had been no detection of mpox infection in Northern Ireland for over 12 months, and, within this same period, notification of clinically suspected cases had been relatively infrequent. “ In the first month of this outbreak, Northern Ireland recorded the highest monthly total of clade Ib mpox confirmed cases of the four nations in the UK. “ In the context of recent UK case numbers, the size of this outbreak – 22 confirmed cases – is particularly notable, given the relatively small population size of Northern Ireland .” Mpox and the types explained MPOX is a viral infectious disease. It is a rare zoonosis, which means that it is transmitted to humans from an animal. The disease primarily occurs in remote parts of Central and West Africa , near tropical rainforests. Mpox causes symptoms between five and 21 days after exposure. The symptoms of monkeypox start similar to the flu . But then a rash breaks out, starting on the face. Initial symptoms include: An itchy and sometimes painful rash slowly appears one to three days into illness, starting with the face, palms of the hands and soles of the feet. What starts as a seemingly harmless red rash – which looks like chickenpox – evolves into angry blisters that can last several days. The inside of the mouth, genitals and lining of the eyes can also be affected by the nasty rash. If the rash spreads to the eyes it can cause blindness. While some patients may have only a few lesions, others will have thousands, the WHO says. Symptoms generally last from 14 to 21 days, with severe cases relating to age, the extent of virus exposure, the patient’s health and the severity of complications. What are the different mpox Clades? There are two distinct mpox Clades: Clade 1 (with subclades 1a and 1b) Clade 2 (with subclades 2a and 2b) Clade 2 (subclade 2b) was responsible for the global mpox outbreak in 2022-2023. Over 100,000 cases were reported across the world. Clade 1b emerged in 2023-2024 and has swept mainly through central Africa, infecting tens of thousands since the outbreak began. Countries like the Democratic Republic of Congo have been hit especially hard with cases also spotted in Burundi, Rwanda, Uganda, and Kenya. The World Health Organization (WHO) declared the clade 1b outbreak a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) in August 2024, due to rapid expansion and higher severity compared to clade 2. They added: “Our experience demonstrates the potential for a rapid growth in case numbers over a short time period and emphasises the need for increased public awareness of the ongoing risks of acquiring mpox as an STI in Europe, particularly during the summer months, when travel-associated infections are more likely. “Continued promotion of pre-exposure vaccination remains important for groups at highest risk of mpox.” Dr Jonas D. Albarnaz, an expert in infectious disease at The Pirbright Institute in Woking, told Sun Health : “The continued detection of cases indicates that some cases remain undetected, enabling the virus to spread silently. “Cases are usually identified when individuals report to sexual health clinics or emergency services due to worsening of the symptoms. “Approximately half of the individuals sought emergency services first, which may have delayed diagnosis in a few days. “Undetected infections, delayed diagnosis, and ongoing community transmission make the emergence of more clusters of clade 1b mpox likely.” He added: “One important consideration of the community transmission of mpox is that sustained human-to-human transmission offers an opportunity for the virus to acquire mutations that increase the efficiency of transmission. “Both clade 1b and II mpox viruses have patterns of mutations that indicate these viruses evolved during sustained human-to-human transmission.” Professor Michael Marks, a professor of medicine at the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine, also said: “Close sexual contact is clearly an effective route of transmission for both clade 1 and 2 mpox. “We have seen following the 2022 clade 2 pandemic that there has been low level sustained transmission in the UK and we should anticipate that this may be similar for clade 1.” Clade 1b emerged in 2024 and has swept mainly through central Africa infecting tens of thousands since the outbreak began. Countries like the Democratic Republic of Congo have been hit especially hard with cases also spotted in Burundi, Rwanda, Uganda, and Kenya. However, experts say fatality rates of clade 1b from central Africa are unlikely to be replicated in developed nations like the UK due to better access to higher quality healthcare. Following the emergence of cases, the World Health Organization (WHO) declared an ongoing mpox outbreak across several central African nations as a “public health emergency of international concern”. Can I get the jab? THE NHS is offering the mpox vaccine to people who are at increased risk of catching mpox. You may be able to have the mpox vaccine if: you’re a man who has sex with other men and you have multiple partners, participate in group sex, or attend sex-on-premises venues (staff at these venues may also be eligible) you’ve had contact with someone who has mpox If you’ve had contact with someone who has mpox, the contact tracing team should contact you. They will check your risk of catching mpox and tell you if you need to have an mpox vaccine. This is the same designation the WHO gave Covid in late January 2020, just a few weeks before the virus ripped across the world. Mpox causes characteristic lumpy lesions, as well as a fever, aches and pains and fatigue. However, in a small number of cases, it can enter the blood and lungs, as well as other parts of the body, when it becomes life-threatening. Current mpox vaccines , which are designed to work on smallpox a close relative of the mpox virus, were used during the 2022 outbreak against the milder strain. But experts believe it does offer some protection against 1b. The WHO and the NHS recommends a vaccine within four days of contact with someone who has the virus or within up to 14 days if there are no symptoms. Healthcare workers and men who have sex with men are advised to receive a vaccine even if they have had no mpox exposure. There are no direct treatments available with medics focused instead on supporting a patient to help their body fight off the virus. Dr Albarnaz said: “MVA-BN is one of the vaccines currently available globally and requires the intradermal injection of two doses four weeks apart. “However, immunity wanes post-vaccination, suggesting that boosters might be required to maintain vaccine effectiveness.”

This is the same designation the WHO gave Covid in late January 2020, just a few weeks before the virus ripped across the world. Mpox causes characteristic lumpy lesions, as well as a fever, aches and pains and fatigue. However, in a small number of cases, it can enter the blood and lungs, as well as other parts of the body, when it becomes life-threatening. Current mpox vaccines , which are designed to work on smallpox a close relative of the mpox virus, were used during the 2022 outbreak against the milder strain. But experts believe it does offer some protection against 1b. The WHO and the NHS recommends a vaccine within four days of contact with someone who has the virus or within up to 14 days if there are no symptoms. Healthcare workers and men who have sex with men are advised to receive a vaccine even if they have had no mpox exposure. There are no direct treatments available with medics focused instead on supporting a patient to help their body fight off the virus. Dr Albarnaz said: “MVA-BN is one of the vaccines currently available globally and requires the intradermal injection of two doses four weeks apart. “However, immunity wanes post-vaccination, suggesting that boosters might be required to maintain vaccine effectiveness.”

news.content_zh: 最近的一份报告强调了英国(尤其是伦敦)猴痘 病例的令人担忧的增加,今年至少记录了 100 例。北爱尔兰卫生官员于 2026 年 6 月证实了“暴发 迅速发展”,并指出这是英国四个国家中每月 Ib 分支 猴痘 病例总数最高的。由于未被发现的感染和延迟的 诊断,暴发 被描述为“悄然传播”,有 5 名患者需要住院 治疗。英国卫生安全局 (UKHSA) 报告 2025 年仅报告 21 例病例,表明数量大幅增加。英国国民医疗服务体系(NHS)敦促符合条件的个人,尤其是与其他男性发生性行为的男性以及最近接触过的男性,接种疫苗。专家警告说,持续的人传人 传播 可能会导致更多的集群和 突变,从而增加病毒的传播能力。暴发 与 2023-2024 年出现的 Ib 分支有关,主要在中部非洲传播,但专家认为,由于医疗保健条件更好,英国等发达国家的死亡率较低。

Conditions A Smuggling Prosecution Over Inactivated Mpox Samples Has Scientists Warning About Outbreak Preparedness Published Aug 05, 2026 11:30 PM EDT By Cole Mercer PASCAL GUYOT | AFP via Getty Images Share on Twitter Share on Facebook Share on Pocket Two National Institutes of Health virologists have pleaded not guilty to charges of conspiring to smuggle mpox samples into the United States, in a case that a dozen scientists interviewed by KFF Health News say has less to do with public danger than with the paperwork that governs how American laboratories study overseas outbreaks. The samples were inactivated. The FBI's own testing confirmed it, and one of the charged researchers helped develop the inactivation technique. That detail sits at the center of why the prosecution has unsettled the infectious disease research community. The practical stakes for households are indirect but real. The pipeline that produces diagnostic tests for emerging viruses runs through exactly this kind of specimen transfer, and researchers say the case is already changing how willing they are to participate. The Case as Charged Vincent Munster, chief of the virus ecology section at NIH's Rocky Mountain Laboratories in Hamilton, Montana, and Claude Kwe, a research fellow working under him, were stopped at Detroit Metropolitan Airport on January 25, arriving on a flight from Paris after nine days in the Republic of the Congo. They were arrested on June 2, when a criminal complaint was unsealed in federal court in Detroit charging conspiracy to smuggle mpox into the United States and lying to border agents. According to the complaint, the two told customs officials that the tubes in their luggage held diagnostic reagents. Each faces a maximum of five years. The Justice Department's announcement said FBI testing had confirmed the viruses were inactivated but that the scientists jeopardized Americans' safety. Jerome Gorgon, U.S. attorney for the Eastern District of Michigan, said the researchers had smuggled viral pathogens on a packed commercial airplane from an outbreak. Federal code requires researchers to register and certify inactivated viruses. The complaint states the pair lacked appropriate documents. Both scientists have been suspended and barred from the laboratory campus during an internal investigation, as MedicalDaily reported. Kwe's federal community defender has said only that his client is presumed innocent and that comment should await further proceedings. The Reason Laboratories Bring Samples Home Studying an outbreak from a distance has limits. Developing a diagnostic test that reliably detects a circulating strain requires working with material from that strain, and validating a laboratory method requires the same. Several scientists told KFF Health News that the specimens Munster and Kwe carried were most likely intended for exactly the diagnostic development purpose stated to customs officers. Tracking viral evolution, evaluating whether existing tests still detect new variants, and assessing whether vaccines and treatments remain effective all depend on access to current specimens from where transmission is occurring. This work is regulated rather than freewheeling. Import permits, select agent rules, inactivation certification, institutional biosafety review and hazardous materials shipping requirements all apply, and researchers typically coordinate them weeks in advance with an institution's biosafety office. The allegation here is a failure to satisfy those requirements, not an allegation that the material itself was dangerous. A Pattern Researchers Say They Recognize The case follows a series of prosecutions involving biological material carried or shipped by scientists, several brought by the same US attorney's office in the Eastern District of Michigan. Earlier cases involved Chinese nationals at a University of Michigan laboratory and a Russian-born Harvard researcher stopped with frog embryos. Reporting by KFF Health News, published through CNN, found that a dozen scientists interviewed characterized the arrests as part of a broader campaign, arguing that any errors involved were procedural and posed no threat to the public. The reaction inside the field is about credibility as much as law. Kim Hasenkrug, an NIH scientist emeritus who worked at Rocky Mountain Laboratories for 31 years, said the episode gives ammunition to people trying to stop this valuable research and sows distrust even among people who had trusted the laboratory in the past. NIH has said it activated established notification procedures and is cooperating with law enforcement, while declining further comment. The Downstream Effect on Detection Speed The concern researchers raise is not about this case's outcome. It is about what other scientists conclude from watching it. If participating in an international outbreak response carries perceived legal exposure, fewer researchers volunteer, fewer specimens move, and the interval between a new pathogen appearing somewhere and a validated test existing everywhere gets longer. That interval is what determines how early an outbreak is caught in a US emergency department. Funding is compounding the problem. Scientists told KFF Health News that cuts to US foreign aid and research funding have left tens of millions of dollars in gaps in the response to spreading Ebola and mpox outbreaks. None of this is measurable yet, and it would be overstating the evidence to claim detection has already slowed. What can be said is that the researchers doing this work say the deterrent is real, and that no formal change to import rules or NIH collaboration policy has been announced. For readers, mpox risk in the United States remains concentrated in specific exposure contexts rather than general community spread, and CDC guidance on vaccination for people at higher risk has not changed as a result of this case. The next developments to watch are further court proceedings, reported from Detroit, and any policy guidance from NIH or HHS on international specimen transport. FBI testing confirmed the mpox virus in the vials was inactivated. One of the charged researchers helped develop the inactivation method. What are the charges? Conspiracy to smuggle and lying to federal agents. Each carries a maximum of five years. Both defendants pleaded not guilty. Why do researchers import virus samples? To develop and validate diagnostic tests, track viral evolution and assess whether existing vaccines and treatments remain effective against circulating strains. Is that legal? Yes, with permits, inactivation certification, and proper declaration. The allegation is that those requirements were not met. Does this affect my mpox risk? No. The case does not change transmission risk or CDC vaccination guidance for people at higher exposure risk. Has anything about research rules changed?
